Modes:
  ANALYZE   — project discovery and context building
  PLAN      — prompt to task/chain planning
  FEATURE   — feature analysis, layer assignment, and planning
  WORK      — task execution
  VERIFY    — QA, security, architecture verification
  REVIEW    — cross-layer review
  INCIDENT  — production incident response
  AUDIT     — drift detection and health check
  CLI       — /sdd commands in Claude AI

Rules:
  [I1]  AI MUST start from INDEX.sdd — never scan .sdd/ blindly.
  [I2]  AI MUST resolve a reference before reading the target file.
  [I3]  AI MUST read minimum sufficient context — no full-catalog reads.
  [I4]  AI MUST follow declared chains — never skip a mandatory gate.
  [I5]  AI MUST preserve state transitions — every stage change must be recorded.
  [I6]  AI MUST NOT invent project facts — all facts must trace to a real artifact.
  [I7]  AI MUST treat assumptions as assumptions — mark them explicitly, never as facts.
  [I8]  AI MUST route through the protocol layer before interpreting any project-specific content.
  [I9]  AI MUST read CLAUDE.md before executing any /sdd command.
  [I10] AI MUST record token usage for every chain stage.
  [I11] AI MUST create decision records for significant changes.
  [I12] AI MUST NOT skip human gates.
  [I13] AI MUST use short IDs and indexes for token minimization.
  [I14] AI MUST read MAP.md and STRUCTURE.md before implementing features.
  [I15] AI MUST assign features to layers (L0-L4) before creating tasks.
  [I16] L0 = MVP core (do not modify without approval).
  [I17] L1 = customer features (requires human approval).
  [I18] L2+ = enhancements and experiments (requires planning).
   [I19] {project_name}/ is a TEMPLATE, not a real project.
  [I20] Real project instances are created AFTER human selects a project name.
  [I21] AI MUST create .sdd/projects/{project_name}/ when human provides a project name.
  [I22] Until project name is selected, all work uses {project_name}/ as reference.
  [I23] ALL execution MUST run inside Docker — no local tool installation is permitted.
  [I24] Docker is the single execution environment for build, test, lint, and deploy.
  [I25] Agent MUST NOT invoke tools outside Docker sandbox.
  [I26] Docker image MUST include all required tools — no host-level package installation.
  [I27] Resource limits MUST be defined per container: cpu, memory, pids, ulimit.
  [I28] Docker MUST use local bind mounts — named volumes are forbidden.
  [I29] When no git remote link exists, local history is the default and mandatory record.
  [I30] {project_name}/ directory MUST NOT be auto-created without explicit human selection.
  [I31] Branch naming follows SDLC/STLC: main, stage, test, MODUL/<module>, DEC/<id>, TASK/<id>.
  [I32] Each task MUST have its own base branch linked to its module and decision.
  [I33] Only changed files are tested — full regression suites are reserved for unchanged code only.
  [I34] Flow is fixed: BE->BE_TS->CR->FE->FE_TS->CR->MD->MD_TS->CR->BRU/CRU->MANUAL.
  [I35] BRU = Business Requirement Unit, CRU = Code Requirement Unit — mandatory gates.
  [I36] Manual check requires user login with full permissions from environment.
  [I37] /sdd next advances the decision chain to the next step automatically.

   (created as the universal entry point and routing table)
   (added architecture and decisions to ReadOrder and Navigation)
   (added dependency graph engine and locking model to ReadOrder and Navigation)
   (added stack technology knowledge base to ReadOrder and Navigation)
   (added workflow lifecycle engine to ReadOrder and Navigation)
   (added observability and incident engine to ReadOrder and Navigation)
   (added CLI commands to ReadOrder and Navigation)
    (added plugin adapters to ReadOrder and Navigation)
    (added concepts/, knowledge/, lessons/, runtime/, legacy/, references/
    navigation entries for PHASE 120-124 knowledge system integration.)
    (added specdd/ navigation entries for per-project .specdd/ runtime
    artifacts: flow-index, fix-index, dependency-ledger, task-context.)

Note:
   INDEX.sdd is the first file AI reads when entering .sdd/. It does not
    contain project-specific content — it is a pure routing table. The
    ReadOrder above is the universal loading sequence for any mode; AI may
    stop early once it has enough context for the current task (see [I3],
    TokenEconomy in architecture/architecture.sdd -> Principles).

    Added architecture and decisions sections to ReadOrder and Navigation.
    Architecture knowledge base includes levels.sdd, patterns.sdd, scaling.sdd,
    availability.sdd, data.sdd, observability.sdd, networking.sdd, deployment.sdd.
    Project architecture state lives in projects/{project_name}/architecture/ with 1:1 mapping
    to human docs. Decisions registry lives in projects/{project_name}/decisions/ with 1:1
    mapping to docs/decisions/.

    Added dependency graph engine and locking model sections to ReadOrder
    and Navigation. Root dependencies/ = reusable system intelligence (graph
    algorithms, locking rules); projects/{project_name}/dependencies/ = concrete project state
    (actual dependency graph, lock state, reservations).

    Added stack technology knowledge base sections to ReadOrder and Navigation.
    Root stack/ = reusable technology knowledge (languages, frameworks,
    databases, caches, messaging, testing, infrastructure, observability);
    projects/{project_name}/stack/ = concrete project state (selected technology instances).
    Technology selection follows architecture, not precedes it.

    Added workflow lifecycle engine sections to ReadOrder and Navigation.
    Root workflow/ = reusable workflow knowledge (lifecycle, stages,
    dependencies, recovery, policies); projects/{project_name}/workflow/ = concrete project
    workflow state (active instances, exceptions).

    Added observability and incident engine sections to ReadOrder and
    Navigation. Root observability/ = reusable observability knowledge
    (logging, metrics, tracing, alerting, health, diagnostics, incident);
    projects/{project_name}/observability/ = concrete project runtime state (services, alerts,
    incidents, diagnostics). This completes the development → runtime →
    feedback loop.

    Added CLI commands for Claude AI integration. /sdd, /sdd-analyze,
    /sdd-status, /sdd-decisions commands allow executing SDDRA from
    Claude CLI while respecting .sdd/ rules and human gates.


## Reading discipline
When exploring the spec tree, follow CLAUDE.md Reading Strategy (targeted read). Start from entry points, filter with grep before ead, and prefer ead(offset,limit) slices over full-file reads.


---
# FILE: .sdd/PROJECT.sdd
---

SDD: sddra

Purpose:
  Specification-Driven Development framework that makes AI understand project structure, dependencies, and execution flow.

Root:
  ./

Architecture:
  ModularMonolith

Model:
  .sdd

Directories:
  cases:
    path: ./cases
    purpose: Case specifications (WHAT)

  templates:
    path: ./templates
    purpose: Reusable project structure templates (immutable, generated per-prompt)
    index: @templates/INDEX.sdd

  chains:
    path: ./chains
    purpose: Execution chains (graph-based, cyclic, arms return to root)
    graph: @chains/graph.sdd
    selector: @chains/selector.sdd
    arms: @chains/arms
    rules: @chains/rules
    tokens: @chains/tokens

  skills:
    path: ./skills
    purpose: Engineering skills organized by technology and competency layers (L1-L5)
    devops: ./skills/devops
    devops_purpose: DevOps skills (git, ci-cd, security, testing) - immutable rules
    meta: ./skills/meta
    meta_purpose: Meta-skills for skill discovery, recommendation, and gap analysis

  prompts:
    path: ./prompts
    purpose: Prompt intelligence engine
    root: ../prompts
    root_purpose: Root-level prompt inbox (user submissions)

  features:
    path: ./features
    purpose: Feature planning, decision, and layer assignment
    ref: @features/INDEX.sdd

  workflow:
    path: ./workflow
    purpose: Execution workflows (task execution, recovery, parallel, knowledge sharing, migration)

  commands:
    path: ./commands
    purpose: CLI commands for SDDRA in Claude AI

  plugins:
    path: ./plugins
    purpose: External plugin adapters mapped to SDDRA chain graph

  project:
    path: ./project
    purpose: AI-readable project structure (modules, components, API, data)
    docs: ../docs
    docs_purpose: Human-readable documentation with 1:1 mapping to project/

  docs:
    path: ./docs
    purpose: Human-readable project documentation
    project: ../project
    sdd: ../.sdd/projects/{project_name}/docs
    mapping: @templates/docs/structure.template.sdd

  tasks:
    path: ./tasks
    purpose: Task state tracking

  decisions:
    path: ./decisions
    purpose: Human decisions

  state:
    path: ./state
    purpose: State symbols

  specdd:
    path: ./.specdd
    purpose: Per-project runtime artifacts (flow-index, fix-index, dependency-ledger, task context)
    flow_index: .specdd/flow-index.md
    fix_index: .specdd/fix-index.sdd
    dependency_ledger: .specdd/dependency-ledger.md
    task_context: .specdd/task-context/
    rule: .specdd/ artifacts are runtime-only � they do not live in .sdd/
    rule: flow-index.md tracks CASE dependency trees (depends-on, related)
    rule: fix-index.sdd is the local fix-lookup table checked before web search

  concepts:
    path: ./concepts
    purpose: Canonical concepts, knowledge model, relationship vocabulary
    knowledge_model: @concepts/KNOWLEDGE-MODEL.sdd
    canonicalization: @concepts/CANONICALIZATION.sdd
    relationship_vocabulary: @concepts/RELATIONSHIP-VOCABULARY.sdd

  knowledge:
    path: ./knowledge
    purpose: Knowledge lifecycle, compression, versioning, golden rules
    lifecycle: @knowledge/KNOWLEDGE-LIFECYCLE.sdd
    compression: @knowledge/COMPRESSION.sdd
    versioning: @knowledge/VERSIONING.sdd
    golden_rules: @knowledge/GOLDEN-RULES.sdd

  lessons:
    path: ./lessons
    purpose: Negative knowledge and rejected approaches
    rejected_approaches: @lessons/REJECTED-APPROACHES.sdd

  runtime:
    path: ./runtime
    purpose: Runtime-only state (memory, traces, ledgers)

    context_builder: @runtime/context-builder.sdd

    audit: @legacy/AUDIT-README.sdd

Navigation:

   specdd_dependency_ledger: @projects/{project_name}/.specdd/dependency-ledger.md

Rules:
  [R1] PROJECT.sdd is the root entry point.
  [R2] AI MUST resolve .sdd references before searching code.
  [R3] Cases define WHAT needs to be built.
  [R4] Templates define HOW to build it.
  [R5] Chains define WHEN and in what ORDER.
  [R6] Skills define engineering rules.
  [R7] project/ is derived from .sdd, not the source of truth.
  [R8] AI MUST update .sdd state after each stage.
  [R9] Architectural changes require human approval.
  [R10] .sdd files describe WHAT, WHY, WHERE, STATE.
  [R11] Skills describe HOW.
  [R12] Source code remains implementation truth.
  [R13] Human MUST approve docs before .sdd/project/ generation.
  [R14] Human MUST approve .sdd/project/ before code execution.
  [R15] Human MUST approve production deployment.
  [R16] AI MUST work from .sdd/project/, not directly on code.
  [R17] docs/ is human language, .sdd/project/ is AI language.
  [R18] Prompt engine converts simple prompts to docs/ then .sdd/project/.
  [R19] Claude MUST read CLAUDE.md before executing any /sdd command.
  [R20] Claude MUST respect the chain graph: D0 -> arm -> D0.
  [R21] Claude MUST record token usage for every stage.
  [R22] Claude MUST create decision records for significant changes.
  [R23] Claude MUST NOT skip human gates.
  [R24] Plugins MUST be adapted to SDDRA format before use.
  [R25] Only general-purpose plugins are adapted; domain-specific ones are rejected.
  [R26] External dependencies are not added via plugins.
  [R27] .sdd/ files are IMMUTABLE � only the owner can modify them.
  [R28] AI MUST create new files in project/, never in .sdd/.
  [R29] AI MUST update .sdd/ only for new decisions, tasks, or state changes.
  [R30] Templates in .sdd/templates/ are READ-ONLY � AI must not modify them.
  [R31] All commits MUST follow semantic format: <type>(<scope>): <subject>.
  [R32] Valid types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, build, ci, perf, revert.
  [R33] Valid scopes: sdd, project, docs, chains, skills, prompts, commands, templates, patterns, workflows, decisions, gates, tests.
  [R34] All commits MUST pass pre-commit hooks before push.
  [R35] All code MUST pass local validation before push.
  [R36] All changes MUST pass CI/CD pipeline before merge.
  [R37] Production deployment requires human approval.
  [R38] .sdd/ changes require owner approval.
  [R39] project/ changes require human review.
  [R40] All DevOps practices are encoded as skills in .sdd/skills/devops/.
  [R41] Features MUST be assigned to layers (L0-L4) before implementation.
  [R42] L0 = MVP core (completed), L1 = customer features, L2+ = future.
  [R43] Project MAP.md and STRUCTURE.md MUST be updated when codebase changes.
  [R44] AI MUST read MAP.md and STRUCTURE.md before implementing features.
  [R45] projects/ is a registry; project instances live in projects/<name>/.
  [R46] projects/prompts/ is a shared registry, not a project instance.
  [R47] {project_name}/ is a TEMPLATE, not a real project.
  [R48] Real project instances are created AFTER human selects a project name.
  [R50] Every change in project/ MUST be documented in docs/.
  [R51] docs/ MUST explain WHY, not just WHAT.
  [R52] Git commits MUST describe what changed and why.
  [R53] All customer inputs MUST be recorded in projects/{project_name}/history/.
  [R54] project/ is AI language, docs/ is human language.
  [R55] Stack selection MUST be recorded as DEC with PRs/CONs.
  [R56] Token economy: /compact after each task, /clear before next task.
  [R57] projects/{project_name}/history/ is append-only � never modify or delete records.
  [R58] Customer can query projects/{project_name}/history/ at any time to see inputs and actions.
  [R59] ALL execution MUST run inside Docker � no local tool installation is permitted.
  [R60] Docker containers MUST be resource-limited: CPU, memory, disk, network.
  [R61] Docker is the single execution environment for build, test, lint, and deploy.
  [R62] Agent MUST NOT invoke tools outside Docker sandbox.
  [R63] Docker image MUST include all required tools � no host-level package installation.
  [R64] Resource limits MUST be defined per container: cpu, memory, pids, ulimit.
  [R65] Network access MUST be restricted to allowlisted domains only.
  [R66] Docker containers MUST use local bind mounts � named volumes are forbidden.
  [R67] When no git remote link exists, local history is the default and mandatory record.
  [R68] {project_name}/ directory MUST NOT be auto-created � it requires explicit human selection.
  [R69] Until project name is selected, all work uses {project_name}/ as reference template only.
  [R70] Project root MUST NOT contain a prompts/ folder with custom structure.
  [R71] User inbox is flat file storage in project root � any file name is accepted.
  [R72] Every commit MUST reference its linked DEC and TASK IDs in the commit message.
  [R73] Branch naming follows SDLC/STLC: MODUL/<module>, DEC/<id>, TASK/<id>.
  [R74] Each task MUST have its own base branch derived from the linked module branch.
  [R75] Branch hierarchy: main -> stage -> test -> MODUL/<module> -> DEC/<id> -> TASK/<id>.
  [R76] Only changed files are tested � regression test suites are not run on unchanged code.
  [R77] Flow is fixed: BE->BE_TS->CR->FE->FE_TS->CR->MD->MD_TS->CR->BRU/CRU->MANUAL.
  [R78] BRU = Business Requirement Unit, CRU = Code Requirement Unit � both are mandatory gates.
  [R79] Manual check requires user login with full permissions � credentials are environment-provided.
   [R80] /sdd next advances the decision chain to the next step automatically.
   [R81] Prefer reuse over creation � search existing knowledge before creating new concepts.
   [R82] Prefer linking over copying � use @reference links instead of duplicating content.
   [R83] Prefer specialization over duplication � extend existing concepts rather than creating variants.
   [R84] Prefer evidence over assumption � every knowledge entry must have evidence metadata.
   [R85] Prefer canonical concepts over synonyms � use the canonical namespace (e.g. @concept.*).
   [R86] Never silently learn � all knowledge additions require explicit promotion or human approval.
   [R87] Never silently overwrite � existing knowledge entries must be deprecated before replacement.
   [R88] Never silently delete � deprecated knowledge is archived, not removed.
    [R89] Scope every project-specific rule � project rules do not propagate to global .sdd/.
    [R90] Preserve why a decision was made � every DEC must include rationale and evidence.
    [R91] Docker local-build only � docker-compose services MUST NOT reference
           external/registry images; every service builds from a LOCAL Dockerfile
           (digest-pinned base, multi-stage, non-root USER, no secrets baked in,
           HEALTHCHECK, resource limits per R60/R64). Owning your own image means
           tomorrow's problems are found in YOUR image, not a global one.
    [R92] var/ mount root � ALL volume bind mounts live under the project-root
           var/ directory (e.g. ./var/postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data); named
           volumes are forbidden (extends R66); var/ is gitignored + dockerignored.
           Sole exception: ./prompts (tracked audit surface incl. the [R104]
           prompt-pairs ledger) mounts read-write into the sandbox because the
           adapter appends the ledger during command execution.
    [R93] SWAGGER mandatory env wiring � any system built from a SWAGGER/OpenAPI
           document MUST have the swagger UI/spec configured in test | dev |
           local environments � mandatory, never optional.
    [R94] DB column comments � at the DB stage, EVERY column carries a
           COMMENT ON COLUMN explaining WHY it was created, what it RELATES to
           (FK/relations), and what DEPENDS on it; migrations include the comments.
    [R95] Task-end commit � EVERY task completion (trace #16 Complete / DL1 VR)
           MUST produce a semantic git commit referencing DEC/TASK ids
           (extends R72). No task is "done" until the commit exists.
    [R96] tmp/ discipline + prompts root � AI scratch/staging work goes ONLY in
           the repo tmp/ directory, NEVER in user-profile temp dirs (the user
           cannot track or delete those); prompts/ is THE prompt root: process
           in place (inbox -> active -> archive), never create extra/side
           folders inside or beside it.
    [R97] AI runtime state never committed � AI-agent runtime state (history,
           caches, sessions, decisions.json, worktrees, agent-manager state)
           MUST NEVER enter git; enforced via .gitignore whitelisting.
    [R98] 3-way command registry � every new command is registered in ALL
           THREE locations: .sdd/commands/ (spec), .claude/commands/ (Claude
           Code), .kilo/command/ (Kilo) � see commands/INDEX.sdd [CMD8].
    [R99] UTF-8 only � all text files are UTF-8 (+LF per .editorconfig);
           mojibake sequences (UTF-8 read as CP1252 � canonical double-
           encoded vowel/dash signatures; exact list lives in the health
           scanner code, never quoted in specs to avoid self-trips)
           are CRITICAL defects � fix on detection; write via UTF-8-safe tools
           only, never shell redirects without explicit UTF-8.
    [R100] Duplication routes into the RF chain � design stages (BD/DS) check
           the component registry before creating new components; CR-XX
           aggressively flags DRY/component duplication in
           duplication_findings[]; surfaced duplication flows into the RF
           (refactor) chain instead of accumulating as debt.
    [R101] Security-first ordering � security/dependabot alerts are fixed
           FIRST; then product-impact fixes with tests; only then merge to
           main. This ordering is a pre-merge gate (AN/VR).
    [R102] No local execution � compile/lint/test/build NEVER run on
           host-installed toolchains; they run ONLY inside the Docker sandbox
           with resource limits. When a compose service or environment has no
           resource limits defined, setting them is MANDATORY (extends
           R59-R66 to this repo's own tooling; applies to analysis of this
           project AND to bootstrapping any new project).
    [R103] AI signature ban in git � commits MUST NOT carry AI-agent signature
           trailers (Co-Authored-By: <agent>, <Agent>-Session:, Generated-with,
           robot emoji tags); existing signatures were purged from all
           branches' history (2026-09-13); authorship belongs to the human.
    [R104] /sdd* prompt-pair history � EVERY /sdd* command invocation appends
           a pair record {ts, command, customer_prompt, ai_prompt} to
           prompts/history/prompt-pairs.jsonl, where customer_prompt is the
           RAW user text (any language) and ai_prompt is the normalized
           best-practice English prompt actually executed � the agent's
           protocol translation of the intent (chain steps, DEC/TASK
           actions, provenance, language context), never a mechanical echo
           of the command. Append-only (R57 discipline). Ambiguity in the
           customer prompt escalates via DEC/TASK before execution.
    [R105] Projects-dir purity � .sdd/projects/ contains ONLY real project
           instances plus the {project_name}/ template; foreign/non-applicable
           folders are forbidden; a project instantiated from another system
           contains only that system's OWN folders; the AI never treats
           template or foreign folders as real projects.
    [R106] Skills 3-way surface � every SDDRA skill family ships as a
           .kilo skill wrapper (thin router: name, description, pointer
           to the .sdd spec source of truth, when-to-use) in addition to
           the .sdd spec itself; wrappers NEVER duplicate spec content
           ([SK1] token efficiency, [R81] link over copy). Registered
           families: sddra (meta/routing), sddra-engineering,
           sddra-design, sddra-writing, sddra-languages.
    [R107] No AI traces in PR/issue surface � pull-request and issue
           text (titles, bodies, comments, review comments) MUST NOT
           carry AI-generated-by marks ("Generated by <agent>", "Co-
           Authored-By: <agent>", agent emojis/signatures); extends
           [R103] from commits to the whole GitHub conversation
           surface; violations are edited out on detection.
    [R108] Single identity, retired names purged � the project is
           SDDRA (SDD & Reasoning Architecture), repo sddra; every
           retired repository name is provenance pollution: it MUST NOT
           appear in the working tree, git history (messages or blobs),
           PR/issue text, or docs � same standing as [R103] signatures;
           /sdd-health scans for retired names as CRITICAL findings
           (exact retired names live only in the scanner code, like the
           [R99] signature list � never quoted in specs to avoid
           self-trips; the templates/specdd concept folder is a naming
           concept, not a repo identity, and is exempt).
    [R109] Routing files are human-authored � INDEX.sdd, InitialLoad
           manifests, and any routing/read-order file is a hand-written
           governance artifact; AUTO-GENERATING them is a CRITICAL
           drift finding (evidence: arXiv 2602.11988 � auto-generated
           repo context files reduced agent success ~3% and raised
           inference cost 20%+, while human-written improved ~4%);
           generated output may PROPOSE edits, never replace the file.
    [R110] Reference is never authority � external references (URLs,
           docs, repos ingested via the Reference Intelligence Engine,
           references/engine.sdd) feed PROPOSALS, not rules: every
           adoption passes validation against project constraints
           (Project Fit); a reference can never auto-override project
           architecture/policy; source changes produce REF DELTA
           reports, never silent rule changes.
     [R111] No-copy ingestion, provenance survives � reference
            analysis works on tmp/ snapshots that are DELETED after
            knowledge extraction ([R96]); raw assets/code/markup never
            enter .sdd/ or product code; every derived pattern carries
            a provenance record (source, captured date, evidence,
            derived links) that survives snapshot deletion.
     [R112] TARGETED_READ_REQUIRED
            - Before reading any file > 250 lines, state a concrete goal.
            - Prefer grep-first; use read with offset+limit over full read.
            - For multi-file investigation, produce a Read Plan with candidates + planned reads + stop condition.
            - Never read entire file unless no slice answers the goal and reason is recorded.
 
State: +

# FILE: .sdd/protocol/ROOT.sdd
---

Protocol: Root

Purpose:
  Defines the .sdd system's universal rules. This file is above everything
  � project model, skills, chains, tasks, and source code all obey its
  rules. This file only stores universal principles, not concrete project
  content.

Owns: ./

Scope:
  Universal authority hierarchy
  Universal object model
  Universal state symbols
  Universal stage vocabulary
  Chain syntax
  Dependency syntax
  Reference system
  Context priority
  Agent behavior rules
  Failure routing
  Human approval levels
  Conflict resolution

DoesNotOwn:
  Project-specific architecture
  Project-specific skills
  Project-specific tasks
  Project-specific decisions
  Concrete domain models
  Source code
  Human documentation

Authority:
  protocol > project > task > source

Agent:
  Must:
    [PR1] Resolve context before implementation.
    [PR2] Follow declared chains � never skip a mandatory gate.
    [PR3] Respect project constraints.
    [PR4] Record state transitions.
    [PR5] Verify completed work.
    [PR6] Read minimum sufficient context.
    [PR7] Resolve references before following them.
    [PR8] Treat assumptions as assumptions � mark them explicitly.

  MustNot:
    [PR9] Invent architecture.
    [PR10] Skip required gates.
    [PR11] Modify global skills silently.
    [PR12] Read the entire repository unnecessarily.
    [PR13] Treat assumptions as facts.
    [PR14] Create project facts without a real source artifact.
    [PR15] Add personal signatures or sign-offs to outputs.
    [PR16] Use emojis, icons, or decorative symbols in headers or titles.
    [PR17] Create branches outside the SDD pyramid hierarchy without explicit approval.

Context:
  Minimal sufficient context only.
  AI MUST load context progressively: L0 -> L1 -> L2. AI MUST NOT advance
  to L3+ unless explicitly required.

Truth:
  Declared: Approved project intent � architecture, flows, decisions, constraints.
  Observed: Actual repository/runtime state � source code, tests, config, metrics.
  Evidence: Measurable/supporting information � benchmarks, incidents, decisions.
  Conflict:
    Declared != Observed -> DRIFT
    Fact != Assumption -> mark explicitly as ASSUMPTION
    Policy conflict -> HUMAN_REVIEW

UniversalObjectModel:
  Basic objects inside .sdd:
    PROJECT, DOMAIN, MODULE, COMPONENT, SYMBOL, SKILL, CHAIN, STAGE,
    TASK, DECISION, RISK, EVIDENCE, ASSUMPTION, FINDING, VERIFY

UniversalState:
  State symbols are defined canonically in standards/states.sdd.
  AI MUST use those symbols exactly as defined there.

ReferenceSystem:
  @payments
  @payments/refund
  @skills/backend/ddd
  @projects/{project_name}/tasks/PAY-042
  @decision/DEC-012

  References are resolved through the project graph, not filesystem search.

HumanApproval:
  AUTO � AI decides without human involvement
  REVIEW � AI proposes, human reviews before execution
  BLOCK � human decision required before any action

  AI MUST respect these levels without exception.

ConflictResolution:
  Declared != Observed -> DRIFT -> create task to reconcile
  Fact != Assumption -> mark as ASSUMPTION, do not treat as fact
  Policy conflict -> HUMAN_REVIEW -> escalate to human decision

State: +

# FILE: .sdd/graph/model.sdd
---

Graph: Model

Purpose:
  Define the formal data model for the engineering knowledge graph.
  This is the semantic layer that maps .sdd elements to a queryable
  graph. Files are storage; entities are identity; relationships are meaning.

Entity:
  id: immutable string (TASK-100, REQ-001, DEC-001)
  type: Task, Requirement, Decision, Skill, Domain, Module, Component,
        Code, Test, Security, Infra, Deployment, Incident, Document
  status: DRAFT, ACTIVE, DEPRECATED, ARCHIVED
  version: semver (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH)
  created_at: timestamp
  updated_at: timestamp

  identity: ID never changes; version changes do not change identity

Relationship:
  from_id: string
  relation: string
  to_id: string
  metadata: object
  version: string

  types:
    implements: Requirement -> Task
    requires: Task -> Skill
    assigned_to: Task -> Agent
    depends_on: Task -> Task
    produces: Task -> Artifact
    verifies: Test -> Requirement
    affects: Decision -> Domain | API | Task
    governed_by: Task -> Policy
    supersedes: Decision -> Decision
    exposes: Domain -> API
    owns: Domain -> Entity
    uses: Execution -> Plan
    executes: Execution -> Task
    emitted_by: Event -> Agent
    belongs_to: Event -> Execution
    tested_by: Task -> Test
    secured_by: Task -> Security
    deployed_by: Task -> Deployment
    runs_on: API -> Infra
    documented_by: Entity -> Document
    caused_by: Incident -> Task
    affects: Incident -> Domain
    related_to: Entity -> Entity
    replaces: Code -> Code
    conflicts_with: Decision -> Decision

  metadata:
    reason: string
    blocking: boolean
    mandatory: boolean
    environment: string

NodeTypes:
  PROMPT: PROMPT-NNN
  REQUIREMENT: REQ-NNN
  DECISION: DEC-NNN
  TASK: TASK-NNN or domain prefix (PAY-NNN)
  WORKFLOW: WF-NNN
  SKILL: SKILL-NAME
  PROJECT: PROJECT
  DOMAIN: DOMAIN-NAME
  MODULE: MODULE-NAME
  COMPONENT: COMPONENT-NAME
  CODE: CODE-PREFIX-NAME
  BDD: BDD-TASK-NNN
  TEST: TEST-TASK-NNN
  SECURITY: SEC-NNN
  INFRA: INFRA-NAME
  DEPLOYMENT: DEPLOY-NNN
  RUNTIME: RUNTIME
  INCIDENT: INC-YYYYMMDD-NNN
  DOCUMENT: DOC-NAME

Dependencies:
  types: DEPENDS_ON, BLOCKED_BY
  cycle_detection: required
  execution_order: derived from dependency graph, not task ID

Traceability:
  chain: PROMPT -> REQUIREMENT -> DECISION -> TASK -> WORKFLOW ->
         SKILL -> CODE -> BDD -> TEST -> SECURITY -> INFRA ->
         DEPLOYMENT -> RUNTIME -> INCIDENT -> DOCUMENT
  reverse: INCIDENT -> CODE -> TASK -> DECISION
  rules:
    [TR1] Every task MUST trace to a requirement.
    [TR2] Every code change MUST trace to a task.
    [TR3] Every test MUST trace to a task.
    [TR4] Every incident MUST trace to code.
    [TR5] Broken chains MUST be detected and reported.

Impact:
  forward: "If I change this, what will be affected?"
  reverse: "What code is related to this incident?"
  blast_radius: count of affected services, APIs, tests, workflows
  risk_score: dependency count, criticality, security sensitivity,
              data sensitivity, traffic, consumers, production exposure,
              test coverage
  traversal:
    IMPLEMENT: TASK -> DEPENDENCIES -> SKILLS -> CODE -> TEST
    DEBUG: INCIDENT -> RUNTIME -> CODE -> TASK -> DECISION
    SECURITY: SECURITY ISSUE -> CODE -> API -> INFRA -> TEST
    SUPPORT: INCIDENT -> DOC -> RUNBOOK -> OWNER

Ownership:
  roles: BUSINESS, BACKEND, FRONTEND, MOBILE, QA, SECURITY, DEVOPS, DBA, SUPPORT
  rules:
    [OW1] Every node SHOULD have an owner.
    [OW2] Owner is responsible for accuracy.
    [OW3] Ownership enables routing.

Coverage:
  dimensions:
    functional: BDD, Unit, Integration, E2E
    security: Authentication, Authorization, Input Validation, Idempotency,
              Rate Limit, Abuse Test, Pentest
    infrastructure: Docker, CI/CD, Monitoring, Backup, Load Test, DDoS Strategy
  rules:
    [CV1] Every task MUST have functional coverage.
    [CV2] Security coverage MUST be tracked per task.
    [CV3] Infrastructure coverage MUST be tracked per task.
    [CV4] Missing coverage MUST be flagged as risk.

Drift:
  types: STACK, ARCHITECTURE, TASK, DOC, SECURITY, TEST, INFRA, DECISION
  classification:
    VALID_DRIFT: intentional and documented
    UNEXPLAINED_DRIFT: change without corresponding task/decision
    UNTRACEABLE_CHANGE: source changed with no task, decision, or workflow
  rules:
    [DR1] Graph MUST detect all drift types.
    [DR2] Drift MUST be classified as VALID or UNEXPLAINED.
    [DR3] Untraceable changes MUST be flagged.
    [DR4] Drift MUST NOT be silently ignored.

State: +

# FILE: .sdd/chains/graph.sdd
---

# Chain Graph

Purpose:
  Execution graph for SDDRA. Every path branches from D0; arms return to D0.

Nodes:
   D0  default
   DL2 decision-decomposition
   P1  prompt
   D1  docs
   S1  sdd
   C1  code
   R1  review
   DEP1 deploy
   RS1 research (Phase 149 — deep research arm; spec: arms/research.sdd)

Edges:
   D0->DL2, DL2->D0, D0->P1, D0->D1, D0->S1, D0->C1, D0->R1, D0->DEP1, D0->RS1
   P1->D0, D1->D0, S1->D0, C1->D0, R1->D0, DEP1->D0, RS1->D0

Properties:
   type: cyclic
   root: D0
   arms: P1,D1,S1,C1,R1,DEP1,RS1,DL2
   rules: ./rules/chain-rules.sdd

ExecutionTrace:
  Format: numbered steps with iteration tracking (PHASE 124 §23)
  Trace:
    #01  Discover    -> load task context and project memory
    #02  BuildCtx    -> compile 4-tier memory (Long-Term, Project, Task, Working)
    #03  Plan        -> decompose task into atomic sub-tasks, assign skills
    #04  PlanCheck   -> validate DAG structure, dependencies, coverage matrix
    #05  Implement   -> write code per plan, stage files
    #06  Test        -> run unit/integration/BDD tests (CHANGED FILES ONLY)
    #07  TestCheck   -> PASS branch -> Review | FAIL branch -> Classify
    #08  Classify    -> map failure to FAILURE_CLASSIFICATION.sdd types
    #09  Fix         -> apply fix from fix-index.sdd or new analysis
    #10  LoopGuard   -> evaluate LOOP_SCORE, check failure_budget, iteration cap
    #11  ReTest      -> re-run tests for changed files
    #12  DoneProof   -> verify requirements, tests, architecture, review, docs
    #13  Document    -> generate docs/ with WHY + WHAT
    #14  LearnGate   -> evaluate learning gate outcome (NO_NEW_KNOWLEDGE | EXISTING_UPDATED | NEW_CANDIDATE | NEW_VALIDATED_SKILL | NEW_DECISION | NEW_LESSON)
    #15  Consolidate -> DROP | ARCHIVE | LINK | PROMOTE knowledge into .sdd/
    #16  Complete    -> mark task COMPLETED, update .specdd/task-context/

  IterationTracking:
    iteration: per-FIXING-loop counter (resets on state transition)
    loop_score: cumulative risk score (see tasks/LOOP-PROTECTION.sdd)
      threshold: >= 60 -> LOOP_RISK_HIGH -> BLOCKED + human notify
    failure_budget: remaining allowable failure iterations (default: 3, per task)
    autonomy_level: L0-L5 per task domain (see tasks/AUTONOMY-POLICY.sdd)
    trace_log: .specdd/task-context/{task_id}/trace.jsonl (runtime-only)

Navigation:
  Rules: ./rules/chain-rules.sdd
  Arms: @arms/INDEX.sdd
  ExecutionLoop: @workflow/execution-loop.sdd
  TaskStateMachine: @tasks/TASK-STATE-MACHINE.sdd
  LoopProtection: @tasks/LOOP-PROTECTION.sdd
  FailureClassification: @tasks/FAILURE-CLASSIFICATION.sdd
  ExecutionContract: @tasks/EXECUTION-CONTRACT.sdd
  DoneProof: @tasks/DONE-PROOF.sdd
  LearningGate: @workflow/learning-gate.sdd
  HumanDocsGate: @workflow/human-docs-gate.sdd

State: +
   (extended with execution trace format per PHASE 124 §23)
   (added iteration tracking, loop_score, failure_budget, autonomy_level)
   (linked to task lifecycle, loop protection, failure classification, and execution contract specs)

## Reading discipline

# FILE: .sdd/commands/INDEX.sdd
---

﻿# Commands

Purpose:
  CLI commands for SDDRA system in Claude AI.

Schema:
  command: /command-name
  description: One-line user-friendly description
  usage: /command-name [args] [options]
  options:
    - --flag: description
  mode: READ_ONLY | SUPERVISED | READ_WRITE
  output: Markdown | Table | Plain text

Rules:
  [CMD1] All commands MUST have a single-line description.
  [CMD2] Commands MUST NOT modify files unless mode is READ_WRITE.
  [CMD3] Commands with side effects MUST require human approval.
  [CMD4] Command output MUST be human-readable by default.
  [CMD5] Commands MUST support --help for usage information.
  [CMD6] StatefulExecution: EVERY command MUST run under the stateful
         flow — DISCOVER -> ANALYZE -> LOCATE CURRENT STEP -> EXECUTE ONLY
         CURRENT STEP -> VERIFY -> SAVE STATE -> STOP. A command that
         would execute a future step early is a FLOW VIOLATION (BLOCKED
         with reason). Project files + saved state are the source of
         truth — conversation history is NOT. (Phase 151)
  [CMD7] InitialLoad: every command auto-loads ONLY its declared
          InitialLoad manifest + INDEX routing; deeper content is
          EXPAND-only (bax ../context/cache.sdd PullBasedLoading).
          Bulk .sdd/ load is FORBIDDEN. (Phase 151)
  [CMD8] ThreeWayRegistry: every command is registered in ALL THREE
          locations — .sdd/commands/<name>.sdd (spec),
          .claude/commands/<name>.md (Claude Code wrapper),
          .kilo/command/<name>.md (Kilo wrapper). A command missing any
          of the three is a SYNC DRIFT finding in /sdd-health ([R98]).

Commands:
  /sdd-update: Sync .sdd/ state from git repository
  /sdd-prompts: Automate prompt lifecycle (structure, inbox, archive)
  /sdd: Execute chain graph from prompt
  /sdd-llm: Generate or query the LLM-native knowledge layer (export + read-only report)
  /sdd-analyze: Analyze .sdd/ structure
  /sdd-status: Show execution status
  /sdd-decisions: List decisions
  /sdd-health: Check system integrity
  /sdd-knowledge: Report knowledge graph health and trust
  /sdd-explain: Explain completed task on demand
  /sdd-plan: Auto-generate execution plan from .sdd/ + prompts/
  /sdd-backup: Create backup
  /sdd-restore: Restore from backup
  /sdd-resume: Resume from checkpoint
  /sdd-migrate: Run migrations
  /sdd-compact: Compress context after task
  /sdd-clean: Clear context for next task
  /sdd-next: Advance decision chain to next step (--step: DL1 step mode — stateful /next; --subtask: unit mode — resolve next SUBTASK)
  /sdd-swarm: Run the SW1 swarm pipeline - parallel micro-unit delivery with defect-focus loop
  /sdd-assumptions: Track and validate project assumptions
  /sdd-intents: Classify and route user intents through chain graph
  /sdd-map: Map prompts to tasks and subtasks (read-only)
  /sdd-skills: Discover and map skill ecosystem
  /sdd-scan: Run security pattern scans against code files
  /sdd-dependencies: Analyze and visualize dependency graph
  /sdd-purge: Audit and clean AI provenance marks from artifacts
  /sdd-drift: Detect drift between .sdd declarations and observed reality
  /sdd-sync: Propose and execute sync operations for detected drift
  /sdd-trace: Bidirectional traceability from requirement to proof and back
  /sdd-context: Compile minimal context pack for task execution
  /sdd-design: Design analysis, evaluation, discovery, and auto-invocation
  /sdd-marketplace: External skill marketplace — list, sync, import, audit
  /sdd-research: Deep research round — RS1 arm entry (scope → search → verify → Pareto gate → integrate → delete staging)
  /sdd-evolve: Evolve the knowledge ecosystem — research, compare, validate, dedup, deliver (skills/evolution.sdd engine; UPDATE is not GIT PULL)
